title: Slack AI assistant: find decisions without rereading it all
h1: a slack assistant that finds the decision in the thread
description: Use Metal to read Slack threads, find decisions and draft replies in chat. Try three routines with source links and clear posting limits.
answer:
**get yesterday's decision without spending the morning in slack.** a Metal bot searches channels, reads the replies and brings you the outcome with a source link. you choose the ai behind it.

keep a catch-up private in dusk chat, or let it propose a reply for you to post. read-only slack access is enough for both.

review.by: lead agent: read against seo/facts, automated gate, independent fact-check pass

og_line: catch up without losing the thread.

app.name: Slack
app.intro: **get the answer at the end of the thread.** the opening message might suggest friday; ten replies later, everyone agreed thursday. give the bot a channel and question so it reads the conversation around each match.

highlight.use: find discussion of a launch date across the messages you can access
collect the recent conversation in one named project channel
read replies before deciding whether a question is still unanswered
include a link back to the message behind a summary
read the pinned instructions before drafting a channel update
identify the teammate you mean before addressing a message
locate the file shared during a discussion
post the wording you requested, subject to the bot's send controls

app.setup:
**start with a channel and reading access.**

connect slack from **connected apps** and select the bot that may read it. slack handles sign-in; the bot never sees your password.

name the channel and any threads to exclude before scheduling a catch-up.

routines_intro: **pick the moment you keep losing time to.** these routines cover catching up, spotting support questions and preparing handovers. send one to your bot and name the channel.

routines.name: yesterday's decisions
routines.message: every weekday at 11, read yesterday's #cresselwick-launch messages and their replies. list decisions, open questions and proposed dates here, with a message link for each. keep proposals separate from agreements. never post or change slack.
routines.output: a private catch-up with source links and proposals clearly separated

routines.name: questions that still need a reply
routines.message: when a new message arrives in #cresselwick-help, see whether it asks a product question. read the thread before deciding whether it still needs a reply. if it does, show the question and suggested wording here. never post or react.
routines.when: when a new message arrives in the named help channel
routines.output: a suggested reply in dusk chat, after reading the thread

routines.name: friday handover
routines.message: every friday at noon, read this week's #cresselwick-operations discussion and pinned instructions. draft a handover here with unfinished work and people named for it. mark missing owners unknown. never assign work or post the draft.
routines.output: a handover draft with unfinished work and named owners

asks:
**a private catch-up only needs reading access.** the bot can draft in dusk chat while posting, reactions and channel changes stay blocked.

want it to post? allow the send action and choose **Ask every time** for an **Allow** or **Deny** card. you can grant a daily amount instead.

careful with **Full access**: a bot there with no sending rule can send up to 25 a day without asking. give it **Ask every time**.

scheduling a message and editing a posted one count as writes, not sends. exclude them, or put "ask me before you change anything" in the routine. channel settings and other writes need that review rule too.
cannot: **find conversations the account cannot access.** a workspace search does not reveal every company discussion.
**post with reading access alone.** it can propose text in dusk chat. posting needs the allowed action and follows sending rules.
**work overnight on a sleeping desktop.** slack events arrive at once, but the bot needs a running machine. dusk cloud keeps routines running.

sections.h: keep the source beside the claim
sections.md:
**a useful summary lets you open the discussion.** ask for message links. keep decisions apart from ideas that nobody confirmed.

the [channel digest routine](/routines/slack-channel-digest) gives you a recurring version. exclude sensitive channels unless the brief actually needs them.

sections.h: follow the link to the work
sections.md:
**keep the reference beside the decision.** the work may live in [github](/integrations/github), or the agreed plan in [notion](/integrations/notion). include those links in the summary.

if the bot needs to open that workspace, connect the app separately. slack access covers the discussion; the linked work has its own access.

faq.q: can a slack ai bot summarise a whole thread?
faq.a: **yes.** the thread action reads replies. ask for those before summarising, especially when the opening message only proposes an idea.

faq.q: will it talk in my channels on its own?
faq.a: **read-only access blocks posting.** if you allow sends, choose **Ask every time** to read each post before it goes out.

faq.q: can i read the catch-up from my phone?
faq.a: **yes, after pairing to the bots' home.** a paired computer must stay awake with dusk open. dusk cloud works with your computer off.

steps: ask for yesterday's confirmed decisions with links
open the confirming reply behind one decision

mistakes.fix: read the replies. they may reverse the original proposal.

mistakes.mistake: granting posting access for a private brief
mistakes.fix: keep it read only. drafts can stay in dusk chat.

worked.intro: invented launch discussion with made-up teammates
worked.before:
beatrice: could we move the demo to friday?
marco: thursday works better.
beatrice: agreed, thursday it is.
worked.after:
decision: demo moves to thursday.

the confirming reply stays beside the decision, so you can open it before changing your plans.

tip.text: the last reply can matter more than the first message. ask the bot to read both.
